title: CloudPipe — Failure Triage
description: Pipeline failures, organised by what a triager actually does: separate root causes from downstream casualties, separate QC-gate rejections from crashes, then read the detail. Skipped steps are a normal outcome and live in their own row at the bottom.

options.content:
### 🔧 What went wrong, and what to fix

Every pipeline step records its own outcome per participant, session and BOLD run. Read this dashboard top to bottom — each row answers the next question.

**Fix root causes, not casualties.** One failed step fails everything after it in the same session, and each casualty records its own `failed` row. The row below separates the two by replaying the per-run chain (`t1w-to-mni → bold-to-t1w → func-preproc → surface-sample → surface-resample`), because the `upstream_failed_step` field is written empty in practice.

**A QC rejection is not a crash.** `t1w-to-mni` and `bold-to-t1w` exit 65 when their own quality gate rejects an otherwise clean run. Those are in their own row, with the gated metric and the bound it crossed. Everything else — crashed, killed, or output missing — is in the hard-failures row.

**Ignore `failure_category`.** The in-pod writers hardcode `unknown` — `classify_failure()` is deliberately not wired in yet (GitHub #67), and the DAG-level recorder that does call it has no message to match on, since Argo exposes no task-message variable. `failure_reason` is the field that carries real detail; the reason-families panel below is the classification, done in the query.

**History is kept, not replaced.** Records are per workflow attempt, so a failure since fixed by reprocessing still appears. Narrow the time range to the batch you care about.

panels.title: Participants with incomplete output

targets.rawSQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT subject) AS incomplete_subjects FROM cloudpipe_metrics.subject_manifests WHERE overall_status <> 'succeeded' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(completed_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)

panels.description: The true blast radius, from subject_manifests.overall_status. This is the number to trust — Pipeline Throughput's workflow status does NOT reflect it: a workflow whose per-run steps failed still finishes 'Succeeded', so subject-level damage is invisible there.

panels.title: Root-cause failures

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT workflow_name, session, task, run, step, CASE step WHEN 't1w-to-mni' THEN 1 WHEN 'bold-to-t1w' THEN 2 WHEN 'func-preproc' THEN 3 WHEN 'surface-sample' THEN 4 WHEN 'surface-resample' THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS pos FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), attributed AS (SELECT COALESCE(min_by(r.step, r.pos), '') AS root_step FROM f a LEFT JOIN f r ON a.workflow_name = r.workflow_name AND a.session = r.session AND r.pos > 0 AND a.pos > 0 AND r.pos < a.pos AND (r.task = 'na' OR (r.task = a.task AND r.run = a.run)) GROUP BY a.workflow_name, a.session, a.task, a.run, a.step) SELECT COUNT(*) AS root_failures FROM attributed WHERE root_step = ''

panels.description: Failed steps with no earlier failure in the same session to blame. These are the ones worth investigating — the number of distinct things actually broken.

panels.title: Downstream casualties

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT workflow_name, session, task, run, step, CASE step WHEN 't1w-to-mni' THEN 1 WHEN 'bold-to-t1w' THEN 2 WHEN 'func-preproc' THEN 3 WHEN 'surface-sample' THEN 4 WHEN 'surface-resample' THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS pos FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), attributed AS (SELECT COALESCE(min_by(r.step, r.pos), '') AS root_step FROM f a LEFT JOIN f r ON a.workflow_name = r.workflow_name AND a.session = r.session AND r.pos > 0 AND a.pos > 0 AND r.pos < a.pos AND (r.task = 'na' OR (r.task = a.task AND r.run = a.run)) GROUP BY a.workflow_name, a.session, a.task, a.run, a.step) SELECT COUNT(*) AS casualties FROM attributed WHERE root_step <> ''

panels.description: Failed steps that had an earlier failure in the same session. Nothing to fix here — they clear when their root does. Root + casualties = every failed step record.

panels.title: QC rejections

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT step, subject, session, task, run FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND step IN ('t1w-to-mni', 'bold-to-t1w') AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), q AS (SELECT subject, session, task, run, registration_type FROM cloudpipe_metrics.registration WHERE verdict = 'fail' AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) + INTERVAL '1' DAY) SELECT COUNT(*) AS qc_rejections FROM f JOIN q ON f.subject = q.subject AND f.session = q.session AND ((f.step = 't1w-to-mni' AND q.registration_type = 't1w_to_mni') OR (f.step = 'bold-to-t1w' AND q.registration_type = 'bold_to_t1w' AND f.task = q.task AND f.run = q.run))

panels.description: Registration steps that ran to completion and were rejected by their own quality gate (exit 65). Counted by joining to registration.verdict = 'fail', not by parsing failure_reason — the reason string differs by step. See the QC row below for which gate fired.

panels.title: 🎯 Root causes — what is actually broken
Failures by step, split into root causes and casualties

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT workflow_name, subject, session, task, run, step, CASE step WHEN 't1w-to-mni' THEN 1 WHEN 'bold-to-t1w' THEN 2 WHEN 'func-preproc' THEN 3 WHEN 'surface-sample' THEN 4 WHEN 'surface-resample' THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS pos FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), attributed AS (SELECT a.step, a.subject, COALESCE(min_by(r.step, r.pos), '') AS root_step FROM f a LEFT JOIN f r ON a.workflow_name = r.workflow_name AND a.session = r.session AND r.pos > 0 AND a.pos > 0 AND r.pos < a.pos AND (r.task = 'na' OR (r.task = a.task AND r.run = a.run)) GROUP BY a.step, a.subject, a.workflow_name, a.session, a.task, a.run) SELECT step, CASE WHEN root_step = '' THEN 'ROOT CAUSE' ELSE 'downstream of ' || root_step END AS attribution, COUNT(*) AS failed_units, COUNT(DISTINCT subject) AS participants FROM attributed GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY (CASE WHEN attribution = 'ROOT CAUSE' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END), failed_units DESC

panels.description: One row per (step, attribution). A `failed_unit` is one failed step record — one session for t1w-to-mni, one BOLD run for everything downstream. Attribution replays the per-run chain, since `upstream_failed_step` is written empty: a step is a casualty if an earlier step in the same session failed (session-scoped failures apply to every run of that session). Work the ROOT CAUSE rows.

panels.title: Failure reason families

targets.rawSQL: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(failure_reason, 'sub-[A-Za-z0-9]+', 'sub-*'), 'ses-[A-Za-z0-9]+', 'ses-*'), '(task|run)-[A-Za-z0-9]+', '$1-*'), ''), '(no reason recorded — pod died before it could write one)') AS reason_family, COUNT(*) AS occurrences, COUNT(DISTINCT subject) AS participants, array_join(array_agg(DISTINCT step ORDER BY step), ', ') AS steps FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY occurrences DESC

panels.description: `failure_reason` grouped after stripping participant, session, task and run identifiers out of the string. Without that normalisation these are near-unique — the same t1w-to-mni failure appears once per participant because the reason embeds an S3 path — and no grouping is possible. An empty reason means the pod was killed (spot preemption, eviction) before it could upload its record: /tmp/step_outcomes is an output artifact, so a hard kill leaves nothing to write.

panels.title: Failures over time, by step

targets.rawSQL: SELECT date_format(date_trunc('hour', from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at)), '%m-%d %Hh') AS hour, step, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Hourly bucket, stacked by step. A single tall bar is one bad batch or one bad node; a flat trickle across many hours is a systematic problem. Bucketed as a formatted string rather than a Grafana time field, because every Athena panel here returns a table — an hour with no failures has no bar rather than a zero.

panels.title: 🧪 QC-gate rejections — the code ran, the gate rejected the output

options.content:
Both registration steps evaluate their own output and `sys.exit(65)` on a `fail` verdict, so the driver discards the outputs. **Nothing crashed** — these need a look at the gate as much as at the participant.

The QC record uploads *before* the exit, so `registration.verdict` is the reliable discriminator. `failure_reason` is not: `bold-to-t1w` records `exited 65`, but `t1w-to-mni` records `expected output not found` because its recorder checks S3 rather than the exit code.

**The gates, and what they mean**

| metric | fail bound | step |
|---|---|---|
| `lncc` | < 0.65 | t1w→MNI |
| `jac_det_frac_negative` | > 0.005 | t1w→MNI |
| `nmi_gain` | ≤ 0 | BOLD→T1w |

`nmi_gain ≤ 0` is structural, not calibrated: the fitted transform scored no better than doing nothing. `lncc` is a fitted constant and has been recalibrated before — a cluster of rejections down near 0.2 is a real failure, a cluster just under 0.65 is worth questioning.

`mask_dice` and `centroid_displacement_mm` are recorded but **not** gated; the rigid magnitude metrics were gated in schema 2.3 and reverted, because they measure field-of-view prescription, not quality. `ice_mean_mm` was a third t1w→MNI gate from 2026-07-23 to 2026-08-11 and was never once evaluated — fireants cannot invert a SyN fit, so the metric was always absent and the gate failed open. It is withdrawn, so historical `fail` records cannot have been caused by it.

panels.title: Which gate fired, and by how much

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT recorded_at, workflow_name, step, subject, session, task, run FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND step IN ('t1w-to-mni', 'bold-to-t1w') AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), q AS (SELECT subject, session, task, run, registration_type, schema_version, lncc, jac_det_frac_negative, mask_dice, centroid_displacement_mm, nmi_gain, rigid_disp_max_mm FROM cloudpipe_metrics.registration WHERE verdict = 'fail' AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) + INTERVAL '1' DAY) SELECT f.recorded_at, f.subject, f.session, f.task, f.run, f.step, array_join(filter(ARRAY[CASE WHEN q.registration_type = 't1w_to_mni' AND q.lncc < 0.65 THEN format('lncc %.3f < 0.65', q.lncc) END, CASE WHEN q.registration_type = 't1w_to_mni' AND q.jac_det_frac_negative > 0.005 THEN format('folding %.4f > 0.005', q.jac_det_frac_negative) END, CASE WHEN q.registration_type = 'bold_to_t1w' AND q.nmi_gain <= 0.0 THEN format('nmi_gain %.5f <= 0', q.nmi_gain) END], x -> x IS NOT NULL), ' + ') AS gate_fired, q.mask_dice AS ungated_mask_dice, q.centroid_displacement_mm AS ungated_centroid_mm, q.rigid_disp_max_mm AS ungated_rigid_disp_max_mm, q.schema_version, f.workflow_name FROM f JOIN q ON f.subject = q.subject AND f.session = q.session AND ((f.step = 't1w-to-mni' AND q.registration_type = 't1w_to_mni') OR (f.step = 'bold-to-t1w' AND q.registration_type = 'bold_to_t1w' AND f.task = q.task AND f.run = q.run)) ORDER BY f.recorded_at DESC

panels.description: One row per rejected registration, joined from step_outcomes to the registration QC record. `gate_fired` names every bound the record crossed and its value, so a rejection can be judged without opening Athena. The `ungated_*` columns are recorded-only context, deliberately outside the gate — do not read them as reasons. `workflow_name` is the key for pod logs at s3://<bucket>/logs/{workflow}/{pod}/main.log, which outlive the workflow in Argo.

panels.title: ⛔ Hard failures — crashed, killed, or output missing
Every failure that was not a QC rejection

targets.rawSQL: WITH f AS (SELECT recorded_at, workflow_name, step, subject, session, task, run, failure_reason, CASE step WHEN 't1w-to-mni' THEN 1 WHEN 'bold-to-t1w' THEN 2 WHEN 'func-preproc' THEN 3 WHEN 'surface-sample' THEN 4 WHEN 'surface-resample' THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS pos FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status = 'failed' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), qc AS (SELECT subject, session, task, run, registration_type FROM cloudpipe_metrics.registration WHERE verdict = 'fail' AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) + INTERVAL '1' DAY), attributed AS (SELECT a.recorded_at, a.workflow_name, a.step, a.subject, a.session, a.task, a.run, a.failure_reason, COALESCE(min_by(r.step, r.pos), '') AS root_step FROM f a LEFT JOIN f r ON a.workflow_name = r.workflow_name AND a.session = r.session AND r.pos > 0 AND a.pos > 0 AND r.pos < a.pos AND (r.task = 'na' OR (r.task = a.task AND r.run = a.run)) GROUP BY a.recorded_at, a.workflow_name, a.step, a.subject, a.session, a.task, a.run, a.failure_reason) SELECT a.recorded_at, a.subject, a.session, a.task, a.run, a.step, CASE WHEN a.root_step = '' THEN 'ROOT CAUSE' ELSE 'downstream of ' || a.root_step END AS attribution, a.failure_reason, a.workflow_name FROM attributed a LEFT JOIN qc ON a.subject = qc.subject AND a.session = qc.session AND ((a.step = 't1w-to-mni' AND qc.registration_type = 't1w_to_mni') OR (a.step = 'bold-to-t1w' AND qc.registration_type = 'bold_to_t1w' AND a.task = qc.task AND a.run = qc.run)) WHERE qc.subject IS NULL ORDER BY a.recorded_at DESC

panels.description: The failures that need a person: something crashed, was killed, or produced no output. QC rejections are excluded (they are in the row above), so filtering `attribution = ROOT CAUSE` here gives the actual work queue. Use the column filters to narrow by step or participant. `failure_category` and `upstream_failed_step` are deliberately not shown — both are written empty or constant, see the notes at the top.

panels.title: ⏭️ Skipped steps — normal, and usually not about failure
Skipped steps, with any failure in the same session

targets.rawSQL: WITH o AS (SELECT workflow_name, subject, session, step, status, recorded_at FROM cloudpipe_metrics.step_outcomes WHERE status IN ('skipped', 'failed') AND from_iso8601_timestamp(recorded_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)), sk AS (SELECT * FROM o WHERE status = 'skipped'), fl AS (SELECT workflow_name, session, array_join(array_agg(DISTINCT step ORDER BY step), ', ') AS failed_steps FROM o WHERE status = 'failed' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT max(sk.recorded_at) AS recorded_at, sk.subject, sk.session, array_join(array_agg(DISTINCT sk.step ORDER BY sk.step), ', ') AS skipped_steps, COALESCE(max(fl.failed_steps), '— nothing failed here —') AS failed_in_same_session, sk.workflow_name FROM sk LEFT JOIN fl ON sk.workflow_name = fl.workflow_name AND sk.session = fl.session GROUP BY sk.subject, sk.session, sk.workflow_name ORDER BY 1 DESC

panels.description: Grouped per participant × session, since skips arrive in whole branches rather than one at a time. `failed_in_same_session` is the only way to tell a benign skip from a cascade: green means nothing failed alongside it, so the branch was skipped for want of input or because the output already existed. A step name there means look at that step first.

options.content:
**Skipped is not failed.** Three different things produce it, and the record cannot tell them apart on its own:

1. **The output already exists.** Reprocessing a participant whose anatomical is done skips the whole anatomical branch on purpose. Work saved.
2. **There is no input.** A session with no usable BOLD run skips the entire functional branch — `bold-to-t1w`, `func-preproc`, `surface-sample`, `surface-resample`, all four, for that session. This is the common case, and it is why such a participant reads `partial` rather than `succeeded`.
3. **Something upstream failed.** The genuine cascade.

`failure_category` reads `dependency` on **every** skip regardless of which of the three it was — it is hardcoded for skipped status, not inferred, so it carries no information. Use the `failed_in_same_session` column instead.

A whole four-step branch skipped for one session with nothing failed is case 2, and needs no action beyond deciding whether that session should have been submitted.

panels.title: 👥 Blast radius — which participants lost output
Participants with incomplete output, worst first

targets.rawSQL: SELECT completed_at, subject, overall_status, cardinality(failed_steps) AS n_failed_units, cardinality(skipped_steps) AS n_skipped_units, array_join(array_distinct(failed_steps), ', ') AS which_steps_failed, array_join(array_distinct(skipped_steps), ', ') AS which_steps_skipped, cardinality(outputs_available) AS n_outputs_available, workflow_name FROM cloudpipe_metrics.subject_manifests WHERE overall_status <> 'succeeded' AND from_iso8601_timestamp(completed_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) ORDER BY n_failed_units DESC, n_skipped_units DESC

panels.description: From subject_manifests, the per-participant rollup written at workflow exit. `partial` means some outputs landed and some did not — the workflow itself may still have finished 'Succeeded', which is why this row exists and Pipeline Throughput cannot answer the question. The unit counts are of failed/skipped step records (one per session, or per BOLD run downstream of registration), so a participant with four bad runs scores 4 per affected step; `which_steps_*` de-duplicates to the step names.
